title: Traffic Experiments Visual Editor and Emergency Rollback Flow
creator: Sana Patel
description: Design a visual editor for running traffic experiments (canary and A/B) with a first-class emergency rollback flow. The editor should let product and platform engineers define traffic curves, target variants, and guardrails; preview simulated user distribution over time; run a dry-run simulation; and trigger a fast rollback that preserves observability context and produces a human-readable diff summary. Scope includes canvas editor, timeline playback, safety-gate integration, rollback confirmation UX, and visual diffs. Out of scope: backend orchestration implementation and RBAC rules (ENG will own integrations).
acceptance_criteria: Canvas: Users can create multiple variants and draw or input traffic curves for each variant
Playback: There is a timeline slider and play button that simulates traffic distribution over the rollout window with tokenized sample payloads
Safety gates: UI surfaces the current status of configured metrics (latency, error rate, quality regressions) and prevents promotion while thresholds are failing
Emergency rollback: A one-click fast rollback path that requires explicit confirmation, logs a named rollback event, and preserves the previous steady-state variant mapping
Diff & Audit: After rollback, the console shows a compact before/after comparison (traffic %, models, routes) and emits links to the trace/metrics dashboards
Accessibility: All interactive controls meet keyboard and screenreader patterns and ARIA labels are documented in the design deliverable
decisions: Use a canvas-based visual editor (drag + curve editor) rather than purely form-driven flows to help operators quickly iterate on traffic shapes
Playback will use sampled request payloads stored in a simulator layer rather than live traffic to avoid production impacts
Emergency rollback is a destructive action with explicit naming and optional post-rollout tagging for audits
Telemetry links will be parameterized so post-action links open dashboards scoped to the rollout event ID
